notes: Seven-branch exact-cancellation candidate (prompt section 8, second and third comparison: added stationary branches). 341 exact linear constraints: center; Theta_0 (10); q=1 descendant moments of branches 0,1,2 zero (10+20+30); leading moments of branches 1..6 equal to the exact stationary potentials C_1..C_6 of the recursion from Theta_0 (20+30+40+50+60+70). EXACT sector table: (h,0) for h=0..6, (0,1), (1,1), (2,1) all EXACT-ZERO; first surviving sector (7,0) at exponent -2.5808898481 with quarter norm 4839.983 (full circle 9679.966; the invariant of every seven-branch family), then (3,1) at -2.7904 (quarter 23524.8), (8,0) 9364.9, (4,1) 1.577e5, (0,2) 1.686e6, (9,0) 3.222e4. F is in Hdot^-1, L^2 and N_s (all exponents >= -2 cancelled). Optimization: 80 Gauss-Newton steps from the min-norm feasible projection of state 131 with objective ||F||^2 + ||rF||^2 on 0.02<=r<=1e4, angular Gauss 160 (bandwidth-deficient per c1-n4; re-evaluation on midpoint 200 gives the same loss to 5 digits). RESULT (FLOAT, midpoint 200): ||F||_2 restricted = 312.2, far part beyond 1e4 (exact sectors) 2.1e-3; ||rF||_2 total 634.4 (far part 34.7); sup|F| = 465 at r = 0.47, theta = 0.41: the inner region is badly deformed because the r^4-weighted objective does not see it. Far better than d2 in rF (2331.6) but far worse in ||F||_2 (d2: 4.989) and sup|F| (d2: 0.105). NOT a closure candidate; it documents that admissibility through seven branches is cheap to impose exactly and that the objective must include the inner region (next: E_2-proxy objective with gradient and Hessian terms).
